title: Boolean and Character Types
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behavior of boolean and character types in C#.
Choose an appropriate type for a simple application scenario.
Read and explain original C# code that demonstrates the lesson concepts.
Predict deterministic program output and identify common mistakes.
Compile and execute a small .NET 10 console example to verify the result.

understand.concept: bool represents logical true or false. char represents one 16-bit UTF-16 code unit and uses single quotes for character literals. Boolean expressions can be combined with logical operators, while the Char APIs classify and inspect character values.
understand.whyItMatters: Boolean and character values are foundational for conditions, validation, text processing and user-interface logic.
understand.analogy: A bool is like a yes/no switch; a char is like one position in a text encoding.
understand.analogyLimit: A char is not necessarily one complete Unicode character: some Unicode characters require a pair of UTF-16 code units.

explain.narrative:
## Boolean values

The bool type has two values: true and false. Comparisons and logical expressions produce Boolean results. Use &&, || and ! to combine or invert conditions.

## Character values

The char type stores one UTF-16 code unit. Character literals use single quotes, such as 'A'. Escape sequences represent special characters such as newline and tab.

## Character classification

System.Char methods such as IsLetter, IsDigit and ToUpperInvariant help inspect or transform individual code units. For full Unicode text processing, remember that a visible character may contain multiple UTF-16 code units.

## Baseline

Examples target .NET 10 and C# 14.

questions.prompt: How many values does bool have?
questions.explanation: bool has exactly two values: true and false.

questions.prompt: Which operator requires both Boolean operands to be true?
questions.explanation: Logical AND returns true only when both operands are true.

questions.prompt: Which quote style is used for a char literal?
questions.explanation: A C# char literal uses single quotes, for example 'A'.
The character '7' is classified as a digit.

questions.prompt: What does a C# char store?
options: Any number of Unicode code points
questions.explanation: char is a 16-bit UTF-16 code unit; some Unicode scalar values use surrogate pairs.
